description: A three-panel composite of calculated Pourbaix (E–pH) stability diagrams for the Fe-Mn-Al-H2O system at 25 °C. Every panel plots E vs. SHE (V) from -2.0 to 2.0 on the vertical axis against pH from -2 to 14 on the horizontal axis, and each carries two red dotted water-stability lines labelled O2(1 atm) and H2(1 atm). (a) "Al: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C" contains Al3+ (upper left), a broad central Al2O3(H2O) field spanning roughly pH 4-8, AlO2- at higher pH, and Al(AIH3) below about -1.0 V. (b) "Fe: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C" contains Fe3+, Fe2O3, FeO2-, Fe2+, FeOH+, a narrow FeO wedge (arrowed, near pH 11-13 just below -0.5 V) and metallic Fe occupying the bottom. (c) "Mn: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C" contains Mn3+, MnO4-, MnO2, MnO4^2-, Mn2+, MnO, and a metallic Mn band below a horizontal line near -1.6 V. One pink circle appears in each panel, placed between the pH 6 and pH 8 gridlines and just above the -0.5 V gridline; it falls inside the Al2O3(H2O), Fe2+ and Mn2+ fields respectively. Bottom text prints the activities: Fe 1×10-10 M, 1 atm; Mn 1×10-10 M, 1 atm; Al 1×10-10 M, 1 atm. The figure demonstrates that under the experimental condition Al is passivated as Al2O3 while Fe and Mn remain predominantly soluble Fe2+ and Mn2+.

observations.observation: The group consists of three Pourbaix diagrams labelled in their titles 'Al: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C' (a), 'Fe: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C' (b) and 'Mn: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C' (c).
All three panels use identical axes: pH from -2 to 14 (x) and E vs. SHE (V) from -2.0 to 2.0 (y), with red dotted lines labelled O2(1 atm) and H2(1 atm).

A pink circle marks the same point in every panel, between the pH 6 and pH 8 gridlines and just above the -0.5 V gridline; the caption states the pink circles represent the experimental conditions of this study.
In panel (a) the pink circle falls inside the Al2O3(H2O) stability field, which dominates the central pH range of the diagram.
In panel (b) the pink circle falls inside the Fe2+ stability field, below the Fe2O3/FeOH+ boundaries.
In panel (c) the pink circle falls inside the Mn2+ stability field, well below the O2(1 atm) water-stability line.
Panel (b) labels a narrow FeO region, indicated by an arrow, located at high pH (about pH 11-13) and negative potential near -0.5 to -1.0 V, with metallic Fe occupying the region below.
Panel (c) shows metallic Mn as a band bounded above by a near-horizontal line at roughly -1.6 V, spanning the full pH range.
Panel (c) contains the labels Mn3+, MnO4-, MnO2, MnO4^2-, Mn2+ and MnO, with MnO2 and MnO4^2- placed in the upper right (high pH, high potential) part of the diagram.
Panel (a) contains the labels Al3+, Al2O3(H2O), AlO2- and Al(AIH3), with Al(AIH3) below the black boundary at about -1.0 V.
Bottom text of the figure prints the calculation conditions: Fe: 1×10-10 M, 1 atm; Mn: 1×10-10 M, 1 atm; Al: 1×10-10 M, 1 atm.
The citing text states the E-pH diagram of the Fe-Mn-Al-H2O system at 25 °C was calculated via HSC Chemistry 9 software.
The citing text states that Al resides within the stable zone of Al2O3 under environmental conditions, so it spontaneously forms a stable and dense oxide film even under anaerobic conditions.

The citing text states the main stable state of Fe is Fe2+, with the FeO stability zone located in the high-pH, negative-potential region, and that Mn primarily exists as Mn2+ under the current environmental conditions.

subfigures.description: E-pH diagram titled 'Al: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C', axes pH -2 to 14 and E vs. SHE (V) -2.0 to 2.0, with red dotted O2(1 atm)/H2(1 atm) lines. Fields labelled Al3+, Al2O3(H2O), AlO2- and Al(AIH3). A pink circle sits between the pH 6 and 8 gridlines just above -0.5 V, i.e. inside the Al2O3(H2O) field.

E-pH diagram titled 'Fe: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C' with the same axes and water-stability lines. Fields labelled Fe3+, Fe2O3, FeO2-, Fe2+, FeOH+, FeO (small arrowed wedge at high pH, near pH 11-13 around -0.5 to -1.0 V) and metallic Fe at the bottom. The pink circle lies in the Fe2+ field.

E-pH diagram titled 'Mn: Fe-Mn-Al-System at 25 °C' with the same axes and water-stability lines. Fields labelled Mn3+, MnO4-, MnO2, MnO4^2-, Mn2+, MnO, and metallic Mn below a near-horizontal boundary around -1.6 V. The pink circle lies in the Mn2+ field, and a small leader arrow marks a boundary near the Mn3+ label.
